clue.text: Ups and downs on this vessel steaming round the equator

parts.note: a tramp is a tramp steamer, a cargo ship with no fixed route
a round shape is the letter O
sailors call the equator the Line

explanation.surface: A steamship is sailing across the equator, with its passengers bobbing up and down on the swell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ups and downs on this' reads as the ship's motion at sea, but it defines the springy gym apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast bounces up and down on this stretched canvas frame.

clue.text: Marsh the artist

explanation.surface: A brief caption naming a painter called Marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Romney Marsh is a stretch of wetland in Kent, England; George Romney was an eighteenth-century English portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Romney Marsh is a Kent wetland, and George Romney a Georgian portrait painter.

clue.text: Musically arranged as to some royal occasion

definitions.text: Musically arranged as to some royal occasion

indicators.note: arranged means these letters are put in a new order, as music is arranged

explanation.surface: Music has been arranged to suit a royal ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles AS TO SOME; the whole clue then describes how music for a royal event would be marked.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction means stately or majestic, fitting a regal ceremony.

clue.text: Speaker admits one snare — he began it all

indicators.note: admits means the speaker's word lets other letters in

parts.note: a speaker making speeches is an orator
one is the Roman numeral I
a gin is a trap or snare for game

explanation.surface: A public speaker confesses he fell into a trap, and claims he started everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder or creator is the person who started a thing off.

clue.text: One thus precludes indications of the pressure

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
so means thus, in this way
to preclude something is to bar it

explanation.surface: Someone says that a certain thing rules out signs of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressure' sounds like stress, but it is atmospheric pressure on a weather map.
explanation.definitionFit: These lines on a weather chart join places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Freeborn character upset most of the rail union

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ASLEF is the British train drivers' trade union

explanation.surface: A free-born figure overturns most of the railway workers' union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freeborn' hides the film Born Free, about the lioness raised by Joy Adamson. 'most of' trims ASLEF to ASLE, and 'upset' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The lioness in Joy Adamson's book and film Born Free has this name.

clue.text: She picked up three golds without winning a race

definitions.text: She picked up three golds without winning a race

parts.words: She picked up three golds without winning a race
parts.note: in Greek myth a swift huntress lost a footrace because she stopped to gather three golden apples rolled by her suitor

explanation.surface: An athlete who collected three gold medals yet never won a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golds' suggests Olympic medals, but they are the golden apples of the myth, which cost her the race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek huntress lost her footrace to Hippomenes by stopping for golden apples.

clue.text: Notepaper designating the principal of the Correspondence College?

definitions.text: designating the principal of the Correspondence College?

explanation.surface: A college's printed notepaper shows who runs the place.
explanation.walkthrough: A correspondence college teaches by post, so the pun makes its principal the head of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed stationery carries a heading; a head of letters would run a postal college.

clue.text: One of Dean Farrar's boy's minor degrees

definitions.text: One of Dean Farrar's boy's minor degrees

parts.words: One of Dean Farrar's boy's minor degrees
parts.note: Dean Farrar's Victorian school story about a boy named Eric is subtitled with a phrase meaning gradually, step by small step, and one such step is wanted

explanation.surface: A question about the lesser qualifications of a boy in a Victorian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: F. W. Farrar's 1858 school story is 'Eric, or, Little by Little'; 'degrees' means stages, not university qualifications.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's subtitle repeats the word for a small amount, each one a minor stage.

clue.text: Before I leave I am favourite — some complaint?

indicators.note: Before puts the first pair of pieces ahead of the leaving phrase in the answer

parts.note: I am shortens to I'M
a favourite is a pet
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Someone about to depart announces they are the favourite, then asks whether that counts as a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' sounds like a grumble, but here it is an illness: a skin infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagious bacterial skin infection is a medical complaint, an ailment.

clue.text: A small pair in the jeweller's window?

definitions.text: A small pair in the jeweller's window?

parts.words: A small pair in the jeweller's window
parts.note: a pair is a brace, and a diminutive ending makes it small, giving a piece of jewellery shown in a shop window

explanation.surface: A jeweller displays a little matching couple of items.
explanation.walkthrough: BRACE is a pair, and -LET is a suffix meaning small (as in piglet), so 'a small pair' builds the wrist ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain or band worn around the wrist is sold by jewellers.

clue.text: The turn of this novice among story-tellers

indicators.note: the turn of means the letters are read backwards
among means the letters sit inside the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A beginner takes a turn telling a tale among experienced storytellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' finds ORYT inside story-tellers, and 'The turn of' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner or learner in any field is a raw recruit.

clue.text: Curtain not designed for cutting things short

indicators.note: designed means these letters are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A curtain that wasn't made to be cut down to size.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortening something by lopping off its end is the act of cropping it.

clue.text: He enjoys a greater degree of latitude in the USA

definitions.text: He enjoys a greater degree of latitude in the USA

parts.words: He enjoys a greater degree of latitude in the USA
parts.note: latitude seems to mean freedom, but here it is literal: someone living further from the equator in the US, as in the Civil War split

explanation.surface: An American who is allowed more freedom than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latitude' looks like leeway, but degrees of latitude measure how far north one lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yankee from the upper states lives at higher latitudes than a Southerner.

clue.text: Pansy provides comfort below the quarterdeck

indicators.note: in a down clue below places the comfort word under the card-suit word

parts.note: read as a quarter of the deck of cards: one of the four suits
ease means comfort

explanation.surface: A flower offers solace to sailors under the ship's quarterdeck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarterdeck' is a ship's deck, but split it reads as one quarter of a pack of cards, a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild pansy, Viola tricolor, is traditionally called by this old flower name.

clue.text: Lacking grace, not at home in a French church

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in means the absent word sits inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: someone not at home is out

explanation.surface: An awkward person turns out to be away from home in a French church.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough, crude manners show a want of refinement and polish.

clue.text: It grows to a fine score about midday

indicators.note: about means the score goes round the other piece

parts.note: a century, a hundred runs, is a fine score in cricket
the middle letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A plant reaches a fine height by around noon.
explanation.walkthrough: A century is 100 runs by one batsman in cricket; 'midday' gives the middle of DAY, placed at the middle of CENTURY.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a small herb of the gentian family, something that grows.

clue.text: Ordered everyone inside for the poem

indicators.note: inside means the everyone word goes within the ordering word

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, meaning ordered
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody was told to go indoors for the poetry reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A verse form of three stanzas and an envoi with a refrain is a type of poem.

clue.text: The man who came to dinner famed for this 19

definitions.text: The man who came to dinner famed for this 19

parts.words: The man who came to dinner famed for this 19
parts.note: the play's guest overstayed for weeks, a lengthy halt, which also names a cricket fielding position behind the wicketkeeper

explanation.surface: A reference to the famous dinner guest of the play, known for his fielding.
explanation.walkthrough: In the comedy The Man Who Came to Dinner the guest stays for weeks. A long stop is a cricket fielder standing far behind the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The play's guest's extended stay is a lengthy halt, and that is also a deep fielding place.

clue.text: No Freudian slip to catch you out

definitions.text: No Freudian slip to catch you out

parts.words: No Freudian slip to catch you out
parts.note: slip here is the cricket fielding position, not a revealing error; any player in the field aims to catch the batsman out

explanation.surface: A warning that no unguarded slip of the tongue will expose you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' is a cricket fielding position, so the player is one stationed in the field, not a psychological blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer in the field, whether at slip or elsewhere, tries to catch the batsman.

clue.text: Anglican to take in class number one

parts.note: to take someone in is to con them
a form is a school class
number one is first, written 1ST, read as IST

explanation.surface: A churchman agrees to admit the top pupil into his class.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a school class is a form; '1st' is written with the figure read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a member of the established Church of England, as opposed to a Nonconformist.

clue.text: Require to make dough, say?

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, giving one sounding the same

parts.note: to knead is to work dough

explanation.surface: Asking whether one must earn money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make dough' suggests earning money, but it is working bread dough.
explanation.definitionFit: To require something is to want or lack it.

clue.text: A small opening in the archipelago, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means the word is spoken, giving one sounding the same

parts.note: a small island found in a group of islands is an islet

explanation.surface: Someone reports a small gap among a chain of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hole, often metal-ringed, for a lace or cord to pass through.

clue.text: Each trial I lost — disorder of the windpipe

indicators.note: disorder means the remaining letters are jumbled
lost means that letter goes missing from the fodder

explanation.surface: A patient loses every trial, all because of a breathing disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes I from EACH TRIAL, leaving EACHTRAL, and 'disorder' shuffles it. 'disorder' looks like a medical condition but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to the trachea, the airway to the lungs.

clue.text: Something laid round one Hebridean island

indicators.note: round means the laid thing surrounds the numeral

parts.note: a hen lays an egg
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Something laid around a single Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are islands off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This small island is one of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland.

clue.text: Heart movement said to be retrograde to the French

indicators.note: be retrograde means the word said is read backwards

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A heart's motion is reported to run backwards, compared with the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a homophone signal, but it is the fodder that 'be retrograde' turns round, giving DIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phase when the heart muscle relaxes and the chambers refill with blood.

clue.text: Having a row, love? A call will end it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Lovers are quarrelling, and one phone call will patch it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it means rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Plying the oars of a boat means rowing it along.

clue.text: The way to separate beds? Misleading up here

explanation.surface: Advice on a walkway between flowerbeds, plus a hint of deception.
explanation.walkthrough: To lead someone up the garden path is a British idiom for deceiving them.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkway divides flowerbeds; to lead up one means to deceive.
